The Grand Loop · Aug–Sep 2026 Route Day by day Moments Dining Budget Book now Practical
Bucharest → Tuscany → Riviera → Provence → Spain → Dolomites → Arad

Twenty-four days.
Eight countries.
One family story.

A village-to-village drive for M, his wife and Aria (8): the cypress hills of Tuscany, a Michelin dinner on a lagoon island, castles above Monaco, ochre canyons of Provence, the coves of the Costa Brava, a night inside the Alhambra — and a Dolomites finale with friends.

24days · 12 Aug – 4 Sep
~6,400 kmof which 1 night by sea
8countries + Monaco
14stays, villages first
3–4 hmax daily drive (2 exceptions)
Why this route

Every wish on the list, in the only order that makes the map work

The route runs clockwise — Italy first, Spain at the far end, and the overnight ferry from Barcelona folding the map in half on the way back. That single trick removes ~1,400 km of backtracking and buys you four unhurried days in the Dolomites with your friends before Arad on 4 September.

01

Short drives, long afternoons

After the opening dash, no planned leg exceeds ~4 hours, and most are 2–3. You drive in the morning light, and every afternoon belongs to a pool, a beach or a village square. Only two days (Valencia→Granada and post-ferry to the Dolomites) stretch to ~5 h — both split by a proper stop.

02

Villages, not cities

You sleep in Tihany, on Mazzorbo island, among Val d'Orcia farms, in Camogli, Èze and La Turbie, Moustiers, the Luberon, Begur, inside the Alhambra walls, in Altea and San Vito di Cadore. Florence, Monaco, Venice and Granada are day raids — you visit, then retreat to somewhere quiet.

03

The ferry is the masterstroke

Instead of three grinding days driving back across Spain and France, you sail out of Barcelona at sunset, sleep in a cabin, and wake up in Italy — a mini-cruise Aria will never forget, which lands you within a day's reach of Cortina.

04

Art without museum fatigue

One anchor per region, none over 90 minutes: the Uffizi, Niki de Saint Phalle's Tarot Garden, a Riviera day from Miró's labyrinth to lunch under Picassos at La Colombe d'Or, Chagall or Matisse in Nice, Gehry's LUMA tower in Arles, the Dalí Theatre-Museum, the Nasrid Palaces. Each visit is short, booked ahead, and followed by ice cream.

05

Michelin nights, family-paced

You eat out once a day at most. Four to five starred tables are woven in — a lagoon island, the Tuscan hills, a Ducasse country inn in Provence with a proper children's menu, the Costa Brava — plus a bookable three-star wild card in Menton.

06

Built around the fixed points

Wednesday 12 Aug departure, Alhambra on 28 Aug, friends in the Cortina Dolomites 1–4 Sep, and a late-on-the-4th arrival in Arad — rested for the party on the 5th. Every night in between is positioned so no fixed point is ever more than a comfortable drive away.

The route at a glance

A clockwise loop, folded by one night at sea

Overnight base (nights shown) Ferry port — overnight crossing Barcelona → Genoa Fixed points: depart 12 Aug · Alhambra 28 Aug · friends 1–4 Sep · Arad late on 4 Sep
Day by day

The itinerary

Drive times are realistic motorway estimates with a break; add border/holiday margin. Stays show approximate August rates for the three of you — treat them as booking targets, not quotes. Dinner is listed only where it's an event; everywhere else, follow your nose.

Chapter I

The Dash West

Two long, purposeful days that spend the "big drive" allowance early — so the other twenty-two never have to.
Wed 12 Aug · Day 1

Bucharest → Tihany, Lake Balaton

🚗 ~970 km · ~10 hStayEcho Residence, Tihany · ≈€200

The one honest slog of the outbound trip — leave by 6:30, cross the Carpathians on the A1, lunch near Deva, over the Nădlac II border and onto Hungary's motorways. By early evening you're descending to Lake Balaton's north shore.

  • Arrival reward: a warm-water evening swim — Balaton in August is 24–26 °C, and Aria gets to end a car day in a lake.
  • Tihany is a tiny lavender-scented peninsula village, not a resort town — exactly the pattern this trip follows.
Buy the Hungarian e-vignette and Romanian rovinietă online the week before; Slovenia's e-vinjeta too (needed tomorrow).
Thu 13 Aug · Day 2

Balaton → a vineyard island in the Venice lagoon

🚗 ~560 km · 5½ h⛴ 30 min vaporettoStayVenissa Wine Resort, Mazzorbo · ≈€350⭐ Venissa — Michelin dinner in the vineyard

Coffee below Tihany's abbey, then the last push west: Slovenia's forests, a blink of Trieste's gulf, and by mid-afternoon the car is parked at Punta Sabbioni. From here the trip changes gear — you step onto a vaporetto and glide past Burano's crayon-coloured houses to Mazzorbo, a walled vineyard island with a handful of rooms.

  • Golden hour on Burano — cross the wooden footbridge from Mazzorbo and let Aria lead you down the most colourful streets in Europe.
  • Dinner at Venissa — Michelin-starred, set inside the walled vineyard where they grow a grape (Dorona) that survives on this island alone.
Chapter II

Tuscany — the hills you came for

Three nights on a farm above the Val d'Orcia, the UNESCO valley of cypress lanes and honey-lit ridges. This is the splurge base with the infinity pool.
Fri 14 Aug · Day 3

Venice morning, Florence art, Val d'Orcia by dusk

⛴ morning boat🚗 290 km · 3¼ h + 120 km · 1¾ hStayLupaia, nr. Montepulciano — 3 nights · ≈€600/night · splurge

Two icons in one moving day — the only packed sightseeing day of the trip, and worth it. Early boat across the lagoon for a couple of hours around San Marco (or simply a slow Burano breakfast if you'd rather float), then autostrada south.

  • Uffizi Gallery, mid-afternoon timed slot — 90 well-chosen minutes: Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera, da Vinci, Caravaggio's Medusa. Under-18s enter free; book the slot now.
  • Piazza del Duomo — the marble mountain of Brunelleschi's dome, then gelato at a proper artisan gelateria before the golden drive south.
  • Arrive at the farm in time for a swim as the hills turn amber.
Florence has camera-enforced ZTL zones — park at Villa Costanza tram P+R or an Oltrarno garage and never drive the centre.
Sat 15 Aug · Day 4

The Val d'Orcia loop, slowly

🚗 ~50 km of lanes, no leg over 20 min⭐⭐ Campo del Drago — Ferragosto dinner

Ferragosto — Italy's summer holiday — so do as the Italians do: no ambitions, just beauty. A lazy triangle through the postcard villages, pool hours in between.

  • Pienza, the "ideal city" of Pius II — pecorino tasting, and the lane behind the Duomo with the valley falling away below.
  • Monticchiello — tiny, walled, and blissfully unbusy even in August; let Aria lead the lanes.
  • Bagno Vignoni — the village whose main square is a steaming Renaissance thermal pool.
  • Sunset at the Vitaleta Chapel lane — the most photographed two cypresses on Earth, ten minutes from your farm.
  • Ferragosto dinner, done properly: the valley's two-star at Castiglion del Bosco, 40 minutes through Montalcino wine country (see Dining) — it closes Sundays, so tonight is the night.
Estate lovers' footnote: two more Tuscan legends sit within reach — Monteverdi's restored hamlet with its restaurant is 25 min from Pienza (casual Zita serves daily, fine-dining Oreade Tue–Sat, tastings €100–150 — book +39 0578 268 146), and the Ferragamo family's Il Borro wine village lies an hour north (Osteria del Borro serves dinner nightly in August, menus €122–132, with a bistro and poolside pizzeria for daytime and pony rides in the car-free hamlet). Either works as a dinner swap — or even as your splurge base instead of Lupaia.
Sun 16 Aug · Day 5

Sunrise balloon, Siena afternoon

🎈 ~1 h flight, dawn🚗 Siena 45 min each way🍝 Osteria La Porta — terrace lunch

The alarm hurts for exactly ten minutes — until the burner lights and the Val d'Orcia unrolls beneath the basket in first light, cypress shadows a hundred metres long. Prosecco (juice for Aria) and a farm breakfast on landing.

  • Lunch on the tiny terrace of Osteria La Porta at Monticchiello's gate — pici with ragù and the valley shimmering below (book the terrace specifically).
  • Then two art afternoons compete — pick one. Either Siena from 16:30, when the heat breaks: the shell-shaped Campo, the zebra-striped Duomo, the Gate of Heaven rooftop climb…
  • …or drive south to Il Giardino dei Tarocchi — Niki de Saint Phalle's garden of giant mirror-mosaic tarot creatures, one of the great child-delighting artworks of Europe (1¾ h each way; open daily in season 14:30–19:30, €15 / €10 for Aria — timed online tickets only, and the daily cap means booking ahead for Ferragosto weekend). With an 8-year-old aboard, the rainbow giants usually beat the Gothic marble.
  • Evening stays light after yesterday's feast — pizza in San Quirico's piazza and an early night.
Chapter III

Two Rivieras

Italy's pastel fishing coast, then the French corniches — sleeping in a castle village and a hilltop hamlet while Monaco glitters below.
Mon 17 Aug · Day 6

Tuscany → Camogli, via the Leaning Tower

🚗 180 km · 2¼ h + 150 km · 1¾ hStayCenobio dei Dogi, Camogli · ≈€400

Roll out of the hills and stop 90 minutes in Pisa — the tower really does lean absurdly, and children from age 8 may climb its tilted spiral (book a slot). Then the coast road to Camogli, a vertical fishing village of trompe-l'œil facades the tour buses miss. Hungry en route? A 30-minute detour lands you at Castelfalfi, the castle-village resort in the empty hills past San Gimignano — Il Rosmarino, its trattoria-pizzeria, is the family lunch pick (phone-confirm Monday hours, +39 0571 890159), with the borgo's gelateria and belvedere terrace to finish.

  • Evening passeggiata along the harbour wall; swim off the pebble beach as the bell tower goes pink.
  • Dinner: whatever the boats brought in — see Dining for the local legend.
Tue 18 Aug · Day 7

Abbey cove morning, castle-village night Splurge night

⛴ Camogli → San Fruttuoso🚗 210 km · 2½ hStayChâteau Eza, Èze village · ≈€650 · splurge

Before leaving Liguria, take the little boat to San Fruttuoso — a thousand-year-old abbey wedged into a cove reachable only by sea, where you swim above a submerged bronze Christ. Then over the border to the French Riviera by mid-afternoon.

  • Èze village — a medieval eagle's nest 400 m above the Mediterranean. Tonight you sleep inside it; when the day-trippers leave at six, the lanes are yours.
  • Jardin Exotique at sunset — cacti, sculptures and the whole Côte d'Azur curving away below.
Wed 19 Aug · Day 8

Monaco for the day, La Turbie for the night

🚗 15 min hopsStayHôtel Napoléon, La Turbie — 2 nights · ≈€200/night

Exactly the pattern you asked for: visit the principality, sleep in the stone village on the ridge above it. Monaco with an 8-year-old is a surprisingly great day.

  • Musée Océanographique — Cousteau's cliff-face aquarium palace; shark lagoon, touch tanks, whale skeletons on the terrace.
  • Changing of the Palace Guard at 11:55, then walk the F1 circuit's hairpin and tunnel — the barriers stay up all summer.
  • Up the hill by evening: La Turbie, Roman Trophée d'Auguste glowing at golden hour, Monaco switching its lights on 500 m below your dinner table.
  • Tonight's option for the ambitious: Mirazur in Menton is 20 minutes along the coast and open Wednesdays — if you're doing the three-star, this is its best slot, since tomorrow's lunch is spoken for (see Dining).
Thu 20 Aug · Day 9

The Riviera art day — Mirós in a garden, lunch under Picassos

🚗 45 min west, hops on the way back⭐⭐⭐ Mirazur, Menton — optional wild card

The Côte d'Azur was the 20th century's studio, and today you drive straight into it. Forty-five minutes west, above the ramparts of Saint-Paul-de-Vence, the Fondation Maeght hides Miró's sculpture labyrinth and Giacometti's courtyard in a pine garden — an art museum that is effectively a treasure hunt for an 8-year-old.

  • Lunch at La Colombe d'Or — the inn where Picasso, Matisse and Léger paid for dinners with paintings that still hang over the tables; fig trees, white parasols, and the Calder by the pool. Book it the way you'd book a starred table.
  • On the return through Nice's Cimiez hill, pick your master: the Chagall Museum (his biblical cycle glowing like stained glass) or the Matisse Museum in its red Genoese villa — they're five minutes apart; 40 minutes each is plenty. Both close Tuesdays — your Thursday is safe — €12 each, kids free, and bus 5 links them if legs are done. (Maeght: 10:00–19:00 in August, €18, under-16s free, no prebooking needed.)
  • Still fresh? Villa Kérylos at Beaulieu — a Belle-Époque millionaire's perfect recreation of an ancient Greek villa on the sea — is ten minutes below your village (daily to 18:00, €15 / €10, with a children's treasure-hunt audioguide and a diploma at the end). Otherwise: pool, Fragonard in Èze, rosé at the Trophée.
Chapter IV

Deep Provence

Turquoise canyon water, a cliff village of faience stars, and the ochre badlands of the Luberon.
Fri 21 Aug · Day 10

Riviera → Gorges du Verdon → Moustiers

🚗 ~160 km · 2¾ h, scenicStayLa Bastide de Moustiers · ≈€400⭐ dinner at the Bastide (children's menu €25–40)

Climb away from the coast on the Route Napoléon into a different France — lavender stubble, thyme wind, and suddenly the Verdon: Europe's grandest canyon pouring impossible turquoise into Lac de Sainte-Croix.

  • Pedal-boat under the Galetas bridge into the mouth of the gorge — Aria captains, cliffs 300 m overhead. Rentals right on the lake beach.
  • Moustiers-Sainte-Marie by evening: a village stitched to a cliff, with a gold star hung between the rocks by a returning crusader — find it from the terrace at dinner.
Sat 22 Aug · Day 11

Canyon balconies → the Luberon

🚗 ~135 km · 2 hStayLe Mas des Romarins, Gordes · ≈€300

One or two Verdon rim viewpoints while the light is low, then west into the Luberon of Peter Mayle's books — dry-stone villages floating on vineyards.

  • Roussillon's Ochre Trail in late afternoon: a 45-minute walk through blood-orange cliffs and rust dunes — a natural playground Aria will file next to the Dalí museum.
  • Gordes at sunset — the whole stacked village turns the colour of honey; viewpoint is on the D15 just before town.
Chapter V

Into Spain

A Roman aqueduct you can swim beneath, then the pine-and-cove coastline where Catalans themselves summer.
Sun 23 Aug · Day 12

Gehry's tower or the Sunday market, then the aqueduct

🚗 ~1¼ h + 290 km · 3 hStayHotel Sant Roc, Calella de Palafrugell — 3 nights · ≈€250/night⭐⭐ Bo.TiC, Corçà — arrival-night dinner

A three-course morning with room for two: L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue's famous Sunday antiques market on the water-wheel canal (8:30–9:45, quick and early), and/or LUMA Arles — Frank Gehry's twisting steel tower over Van Gogh's town, contemporary art's wildest new campus, with Carsten Höller's giant slides corkscrewing down the atrium. It's open daily 10:00–19:30, and the best parts are free — tower, terraces and the slides (110 cm minimum: Aria qualifies, and adults can race her down); exhibitions €15, under-26s free. Then the day's centrepiece:

  • Pont du Gard — the 2,000-year-old, 49-metre aqueduct, 30 minutes from Arles. Bring swimsuits: families float in the Gardon river directly beneath the arches. (The guided canoe descent from Collias is the upgrade — but with Bo.TiC tonight, save it for a lighter year.)
  • Cross the border by late afternoon; by evening you're on the lantern-lit beach promenade of Calella de Palafrugell, gin-clear water lapping at whitewashed arches.
  • Arrival-night event: the two-star Bo.TiC is 20 minutes inland and Sunday is its open night (it closes Mon–Tue in August) — book ~20:00 and keep the Pont du Gard stop to a swim rather than the full canoe descent.
Mon 24 Aug · Day 13

Dalí's madhouse, then the coves

🚗 Figueres 55 min each way

The Dalí Theatre-Museum in Figueres is the art museum children rank first and critics second — a crimson castle topped with eggs, where a sofa is a face and a taxi rains indoors. Go at opening, beat the heat and the queues.

  • Afternoon: the Camí de Ronda — the old smugglers' path from Calella to Llafranc, 30 shaded minutes above snorkel-clear coves, ice cream at the far end.
  • Swim at Tamariu, the quietest of the three bays.
  • Tonight stays easy — you had the big table last night. Feet-in-the-sand fried fish on Calella's promenade, or Casamar's terrace in Llafranc if you want one more serious plate (phone-confirm its Monday opening).
Tue 25 Aug · Day 14

A day that belongs entirely to the sea

🚗 zero — the car rests

The extra Spanish day you claimed from the mountains, spent exactly as intended: no museum, no transfer, just the Costa Brava doing its thing.

  • Morning kayak or SUP on Aiguablava's improbably blue cove — rentals on the beach; Aria's front-seat day.
  • Walk the other arm of the Camí de Ronda, or claim a cala early and stay planted — Illa Roja and Sa Riera to the north are the locals' picks.
  • Sunset from Begur castle ruins above town; dinner casual in Begur's old town (Bo.TiC closes Tuesdays — the calendar planned around it).
Wed 26 Aug · Day 15

Costa Brava → Valencia's ocean planet

🚗 ~460 km · 4¼ hStayBarceló Valencia (facing the City of Arts) · ≈€175

One last cove swim at Aiguablava's absurdly blue water, then the coastal motorway south, skirting Barcelona entirely. By late afternoon, Valencia's City of Arts & Sciences rises like a landed fleet of starships.

  • L'Oceanogràfic — Europe's largest aquarium: beluga whales, a walk-through shark tunnel, and the underwater restaurant dome. Evening sessions run late in August; it's magical after dark.
  • Night walk through Calatrava's glowing white structures — a whole different kind of "art museum".
A functional city night, deliberately placed to split the long ride to Granada — hotel is beside the park, no old-town driving.
Chapter VI

Andalusia — sleeping inside the Alhambra

The trip's deepest splurge: two nights in the 15th-century convent within the Alhambra's walls, with the palaces at your doorstep before the day visitors arrive.
Thu 27 Aug · Day 16

South to Granada Splurge nights

🚗 ~500 km · 4¾ hStayParador de Granada — inside the Alhambra, 2 nights · ≈€500/night · splurge

The longest inland day — but it starts with a once-in-a-lifetime lunch: paella where paella was invented. El Palmar, a lagoon village 20 minutes south of your hotel, is the dish's birthplace, and Arrocería Maribel — the village's Michelin Bib Gourmand — serves its D.O. Albufera rice by the canal (pre-order when you book). Then the motorway sweeps through olive seas into Granada, the Sierra Nevada standing behind it.

  • Prefer an earlier Granada arrival? Skip the paella, grab the road, and stretch legs at Xàtiva's double-crested castle instead.
  • Drive straight through the Alhambra's own gate to check in — you are sleeping inside the monument.
  • Evening: taxi down, wander the Albaicín's whitewashed lanes to Mirador de San Nicolás for the sunset every guidebook promises — the Alhambra igniting red against snow-dusted mountains.
  • Granada still serves a free tapa with every drink — dinner solves itself.
Fri 28 Aug · Day 17

The Alhambra, properly

🎟 Nasrid Palaces — timed entry, booked ahead⭐ Faralá — star + live flamenco (option)

Your fixed point, honoured in full. Enter at your Nasrid Palaces slot before the heat: the Court of the Lions' forest of columns, stucco carved like frozen lace, reflecting pools built to double the architecture.

  • Generalife gardens — fountains, cypress tunnels and shade; let Aria hunt for the water staircase with cool streams running inside its banisters.
  • Siesta at the Parador (this is why you sleep here), then the Alcazaba ramparts at soft light.
  • Evening: a zambra in the Sacromonte caves — flamenco in the whitewashed grottoes where it was born; early shows welcome families.
Chapter VII

The sea road home

Two beach-paced driving days up the coast, then the trick that folds the map: a ship swallows the car in Barcelona and spits it out in Italy.
Sat 29 Aug · Day 18

Granada → Altea's white old town

🚗 ~390 km · 3¾ hStayHotel Cap Negret, Altea · ≈€175

Down from the mountains and back to the Mediterranean at Altea — the Costa Blanca's prettiest old town, a hill of white lanes under a blue-tiled dome, somehow untouched by the concrete around Benidorm.

  • Afternoon on the beach; evening climbing the flowered lanes to the church square for dinner with the sea below.
Sun 30 Aug · Day 19

Roman lunch, sunset sailaway

🚗 ~470 km · 4½ hStayGNV outside cabin, car + 3 · ≈€450–650 all-in

North along the coast with a two-hour stop in Tarragona — its Roman amphitheatre sits right on the sea, gladiator arena with a beach view. Then Barcelona's port, where the car disappears into the hull.

  • Sailaway from the deck: Barcelona, Montjuïc and the whole Catalan coast shrinking in gold light while Aria checks every corner of the ship.
  • Cabin sleep in your own beds at sea — tomorrow, Italy.
Mon 31 Aug · Day 20

A day at sea, an evening in Italy

⛴ ~20 h at seaStayBW Regina Elena, Santa Margherita · ≈€270

Breakfast with dolphins if you're lucky, pool deck, card games, absolutely no driving. GNV's Barcelona–Genoa crossing runs about 20 hours; depending on the sailing you dock in Genoa between late afternoon and evening. A short hop from the port and you're eating gelato on a Riviera promenade one last time.

Ferry schedules firm up when booking opens — if the sailing lands early enough, push on to Lake Garda instead and shorten tomorrow by two hours. Both options are pre-listed in Stays.
Chapter VIII

Dolomites with friends

Three nights in San Vito di Cadore below the pale walls of Antelao and Pelmo — Cortina ten minutes away, two full mountain days, and a hike for each of them.
Tue 1 Sep · Day 21

North to San Vito di Cadore

🚗 ~470 km · ~5 h, split by Lake Garda lunchStayParkhotel Ladinia, San Vito — 3 nights half-board · ≈€320/night

The last real transfer, broken at Sirmione — a castle on a spit in Lake Garda, lunch by the drawbridge. Then the Autostrada climbs past Belluno and the Dolomites' rock towers start filling the windscreen.

  • Arrive mid-afternoon; aperitivo with your friends as Antelao — the "King of the Dolomites" — pinks up over the village at sunset.
  • Ambitions for the week sorted over dinner: the turquoise Lago di Sorapis (pictured) hides 20 minutes away for the sure-footed grown-ups, but the two family days below are the plan.
Wed 2 Sep · Day 22

Hike day — Tre Cime di Lavaredo

🚗 50 min to Misurina🥾 ~10 km loop · 3½–4 h · easy-moderate

The Dolomites' signature walk: the full circuit of the three great stone teeth, on wide military paths with rifugio stops for spremuta and strudel — lunch mid-hike at Rifugio Locatelli, facing the north walls. Fit eight-year-olds do it proudly, and early September means the summer crowds are gone.

  • Go early — the toll road needs a licence-plate reservation (book for today) and parking fills by 9.
  • Afternoon reward: Lago di Misurina's shoreline, then gelato in Cortina's Corso Italia on the way home.
Thu 3 Sep · Day 23

Emerald water, five towers, one farewell

🚗 Braies 1 h · Cinque Torri 30 min🚣 rowboat + chairlift + trench walk⭐ SanBrite, Cortina — farewell dinner

The grand finale, in three acts. At first light, Lago di Braies: take out a wooden rowboat before the day fills — emerald water, a wall of rock, the photo that hangs in your hallway. Be through the valley before the 9:00 road-restriction window (it runs to 15 Sep) or pre-book parking; boats go out from 8:00.

  • Act two, on the way back: the chairlift up to the Cinque Torri — five freestanding towers ringed by restored WWI trenches you walk straight through, history lesson turned adventure playground. Rifugio Averau, arguably the best mountain-hut table in the Alps, is 30 minutes' walk beyond if the group votes for a big lunch.
  • Act three: spa hour back at the hotel, then the farewell dinner with the whole group — Cortina's starred farmhouse if you book it, its casual sister farm if you don't (see Dining).
Chapter IX

Home stretch

Fri 4 Sep · Day 24

San Vito di Cadore → Arad

🚗 ~1,000 km · 10–11 h with borders

The second and last permitted monster — but with the party on the 5th, a late-evening arrival on the 4th is exactly the plan. A civilised 7:30 start, out through the Cadore valleys to Lienz, then Villach – Graz – Budapest – Szeged and across at Nădlac: Arad by ~21:00 with proper lunch and coffee stops, in bed before midnight, fresh for tomorrow.

Keep the last Dolomites morning intact — Braies at dawn on the 3rd stays, and there's even time for a farewell breakfast with your friends on the 4th before rolling out.
Once in a lifetime

The moments this trip is really about

For everyone

A balloon over the Val d'Orcia

Sunrise flight above the cypress lanes you fell in love with — one hour aloft, prosecco and farm breakfast on landing.

For everyone

Sleeping inside the Alhambra

When the gates close, the hill empties — and you're still there, in a 15th-century convent between the palaces and the Generalife.

For the grown-ups

A Michelin star on a vineyard island

Dinner inside Mazzorbo's walled vineyard, boats for taxis, Burano's colours across the footbridge.

For the album

Rowing on Lago di Braies

A wooden boat on glass-green water under a wall of Dolomite rock — earned by a dawn start, shared with your friends.

For Aria

Swimming under a Roman aqueduct

Two thousand years of engineering overhead, cool river water below. History class, cancelled forever.

For Aria

The ship that swallows the car

Drive into a nine-deck ship, sleep in a cabin at sea, wake up in a different country. Better than any bedtime story.

For the grown-ups

A castle village after the crowds leave

Èze at 7 p.m. belongs to the people sleeping in it — lanes of gold stone and the whole Riviera below your window.

For Aria

Dalí's theatre of wonders

A museum where it rains inside a taxi and a room becomes a face — the day she decides art is actually amazing.

Tables worth planning around

Michelin stars & honest legends

One meal out per day, remember — so these are the days when that meal is the event. Book the starred ones the moment dates firm up; children are welcome at every table below.

Venissa

★ MICHELIN
Mazzorbo island, Venice lagoon — dinner, Thu 13 Aug

Tasting menus built on lagoon fish, island vegetables and the walled vineyard around your table — you sleep thirty metres away. Two blind tasting menus — €150 (7 courses) or €175 (10), ~2025 pricing — from chefs Chiara Pavan and Francesco Brutto, 1★ plus a green star for the estate's lagoon agriculture. One flag: 13 Aug is their first service after the summer break, so email to confirm — and know that the estate's own Osteria Contemporanea (open daily, à la carte, ~€45–70 pp) is the relaxed same-vineyard plan B that Aria may actually prefer.

Closed Tue–Wed · dinner 19:30–21:00 · book at venissa.superbexperience.com the moment 2026 dates load · no published minimum age — mention Aria by email (info@venissa.it).

Campo del Drago

★★ MICHELIN
Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco, Montalcino — dinner, Sat 15 Aug

The Val d'Orcia's own two-star, forty minutes through Brunello country from your farm: chef Matteo Temperini's Tuscan produce cooking inside a 1,700-hectare Montalcino estate. Dinner-only, closed Sun–Mon — which makes Ferragosto Saturday your slot.

Chef's menu €200 · 3 courses à la carte €180 · smart casual · no published minimum age — confirm Aria when booking (+39 0577 1913001 / SevenRooms) · book 4–8 weeks ahead and reconfirm the Ferragosto-Saturday service.

Osteria La Porta

local legend
Monticchiello, Val d'Orcia — lunch, Sun 16 Aug

A tiny terrace at the gate of a walled village, pici with ragù and the valley shimmering below. The definition of a €40 meal you remember for years. Open daily in season, 12:00–15:00.

Book the terrace days ahead — Ferragosto weekend.

DaV Mare

Michelin Guide
Portofino piazzetta — dinner, Mon 17 Aug

The Cerea family (of three-star Da Vittorio) cooking Ligurian seafood on the world's most famous little square — open seven days in season, sharing plates made for families. Splashy, yes; unforgettable, also yes.

≈€100+ pp adults · book well ahead (Ferragosto week) · davmare.com. Cheaper honest alternative: La Cucina di Nonna Nina in San Rocco di Camogli (phone-confirm Monday opening).

La Colombe d'Or

the legend
Saint-Paul-de-Vence — lunch, Thu 20 Aug

Not a star — an institution. The inn where broke painters paid in canvases: you eat the famous hors-d'œuvres basket on a fig-shaded terrace with Picassos, Légers and a Calder mobile for company. The anchor of your Riviera art day.

No online booking exists — phone +33 4 93 32 80 02 or contact@la-colombe-dor.com 3–4+ weeks ahead for a summer terrace table · hors-d'œuvres platter €40, mains €22–65 (≈€70–110 pp) · open daily in season, families routinely at lunch (confirm Aria when booking) · set her hunting for César's golden thumb.

Mirazur — the wild card

★★★ MICHELIN
Menton — dinner Wed 19 Aug (optional; lunch slots too)

Mauro Colagreco's garden-fed universe menu, once ranked the best restaurant in the world, 20 minutes from your La Turbie bed. As of mid-July, tables for three on 19–21 Aug were still open — rare and tempting. A "Tribute to the Tomato" menu (€380) runs exactly from 18 Aug. Wednesday evening is its slot now that Thursday lunch belongs to La Colombe d'Or.

Universe menu €450 pp · closed Mondays in Aug · card guarantee, free cancellation until 15 days out · email reservation@mirazur.fr to confirm an 8-year-old and half portions. Skip guilt-free — the Moustiers inn the next night has a star too.

La Bastide de Moustiers

★ MICHELIN · green star
Moustiers-Sainte-Marie — dinner, Fri 21 Aug (you sleep here)

Alain Ducasse's Provençal farmhouse: the menu walks in each morning from its own 2,000 m² kitchen garden. Gentle, garden-side, and genuinely child-welcoming — the easiest starred dinner of the trip.

Menus €90–120 · children's menu €25–40 · last seating 20:30 · Friday is a normal service day · +33 4 92 70 47 47.

Bo.TiC

★★ MICHELIN
Corçà, 20 min inland — dinner, Sun 23 Aug

The Empordà's two-star: Albert Sastregener's playful, deeply Catalan tasting menus in a converted carriage workshop. Sunday evening is the night it's open on your dates (closed Mon–Tue in August) — so it becomes the arrival-night event.

Menus €90 / €190 / €250, taken by the whole table · booking form accepts children — email restaurant@bo-tic.com to confirm Aria · book 19:45–20:00 · Monday fallback: Casamar's terrace in Llafranc (ex-star, à la carte €18–32 — phone-confirm Monday opening, +34 972 300 104).

Arrocería Maribel

Bib Gourmand · the birthplace
El Palmar, L'Albufera lagoon — lunch, Thu 27 Aug

Paella comes from these rice-lagoon villages, full stop — and Maribel is the village's Michelin Bib Gourmand, serving D.O. Albufera rices on a canal-front terrace with its own parking. The €42 tasting of lagoon dishes needs a day's notice. (Bon Aire, champion of Sueca's paella contest, is the equally famous neighbour.)

À la carte ~€30–45 pp · lunch only, last seating 16:15 · closed Wednesdays (your Thursday is safe) · pre-order the rice when reserving: arroceriamaribel.com, +34 961 620 060.

Faralá

★ MICHELIN · new 2026
Cuesta de Gomérez, Granada — dinner & live flamenco, Fri 28 Aug (choose your evening)

Granada's first-ever Michelin star, won this year: haute Andalusian cooking staged around live flamenco, on the lane that climbs to the Alhambra — an all-female team, guitar and cante between courses, arrival at a kid-workable 19:00. It competes with the Sacromonte cave zambra for the same evening; the caves are rawer, Faralá is dinner-and-show in one.

Menus €78–128 · no children's menu but no age limit — fine for a good eater · it took 180 bookings in 24 h when the star landed, so book weeks ahead: reservas@restaurantefarala.com · traditional alternative with Alhambra views: Mirador de Morayma (~€35–50 pp).

Rifugio Averau

gourmet hut · 2,413 m
Above Cinque Torri — lunch option, Thu 3 Sep

Named among the ten best mountain restaurants in the Alps: hand-made pappardelle and a 170-label cellar, reached by chairlift and a 30-minute walk. Fair warning for your one-meal rule: it shares the final day with SanBrite — let the group pick one, or declare the last day a two-table holiday.

Primi €15–17, mains to €32 · kids' pasta €15 · open to 25 Sep · reserve by phone +39 0436 4660.

SanBrite

★ MICHELIN · green star
Cortina d'Ampezzo — farewell dinner, Thu 3 Sep

An "agri-restaurant" above Cortina: their own dairy, their own farm, spaghetti steeped in mountain-pine. The right full stop for the trip — with your friends around the table.

Menus €170 / €200 pp (whole table) · Thu is dinner-only; closed Wed · book via sanbrite.superbexperience.com and email ahead about Aria · casual sister spot El Brite de Larieto is the fallback with kids.
Budget

Where the money goes

CategoryWhat's insideEstimate
Stays — 22 hotel nights16 nights of village & farm stays averaging ~€250, plus your chosen splurges: 3 nights at Lupaia (~€600), Château Eza (~€650) and 2 nights at the Parador de Granada (~€500). The three Dolomites nights are half-board — dinners included.€7,400 – 8,300
Ferry — the floating hotel nightGNV Barcelona → Genoa: car + three passengers + private outside cabin.€450 – 650
Road~6,400 km of fuel (≈€850 at 7.5 L/100 km), Italian + French tolls (≈€200), HU/SI/AT vignettes + rovinietă (≈€75), parking & garages (≈€180), Crit'Air sticker.€1,250 – 1,400
ExperiencesBalloon for three (~€730), Alhambra (~€45), Oceanogràfic (~€118), Monaco Océanographique (~€59), Uffizi (~€58), Dalí (~€44), the art trail — Maeght, Chagall/Matisse, Villa Kérylos, Tarot Garden, LUMA (~€165 combined, kids mostly free), Pont du Gard (~€30), flamenco (~€72), Tre Cime road (~€40), Braies parking + boat (~€90), Cortina lifts (~€70), boats & vaporetti (~€100).≈ €1,650
FoodYour one-meal-a-day rule: ~5 starred events for three (≈€1,700 total) + everyday tables, picnics and gelato on the other days (≈€80/day).€3,200 – 3,700
Whole trip, all-in24 days, three people, no corners cut where it counts.≈ €14,000 – 15,500

Levers if you want to trim: swap Lupaia for Agriturismo Terrapille — the "Gladiator hill" farm below Pienza with the same views and pool at ~€250 (–€1,000); make Èze a third La Turbie night (–€450); skip Mirazur and let the Bastide carry the French flag (–€900+). None of the once-in-a-lifetime moments for Aria — balloon, aqueduct swim, rowboats, aquarium, the ship — costs more than €250 for the whole family.

Book these now

The reservation checklist, in order of urgency

Book now
Alhambra — general daytime tickets for Fri 28 Aug, official site only (tickets.alhambra-patronato.es). ~€22 pp; Aria under 12 is free but needs her own QR ticket reserved with yours. August sells out weeks ahead and the Nasrid Palaces time slot is strict. Bring passports — they're checked at the gate.Pick a morning Nasrid slot (8:30–10:00) to beat the heat.
Book now
The three splurge stays — Parador de Granada (27–29 Aug), the Èze castle hotel (18 Aug) and the Val d'Orcia farmhouse (14–17 Aug). These are the scarcest beds of the whole route in August.Then fill in the standard nights; everything else has alternatives.
~3 months out
GNV ferry Barcelona → Genoa, ~Sun 30 Aug, car + outside family cabin (gnv.it). Sails 3–4 days/week in high season — confirm the exact late-August sailing days the moment the calendar opens and lock the cabin (≈€450–650 for the three of you + car). Grimaldi's Barcelona→Civitavecchia is the fallback.If the sailing lands in Genoa early, upgrade the post-ferry night from Liguria to Lake Garda.
6–8 weeks out
Sunrise balloon over the Val d'Orcia (ballooningintuscany.com, Montisi launch site) for 15 or 16 Aug — book both a primary and keep the spare morning free for weather. ~€260 adult / €210 child. ⚠ Minimum height 140 cm as well as age 7 — measure Aria first; if she's under it, ask about a private basket (€1,250) or the Siena/Chianti operators.Full prepayment, free cancellation ≥30 days.
6 weeks out
Crit'Air sticker for the French Riviera — Nice's low-emission zone is active and camera-enforced for foreign cars. Order only at certificat-air.gouv.fr (~€5 shipped abroad, takes weeks to arrive; the email receipt is interim proof).Monaco and Menton have no zone; the sticker covers your Nice museum run.
1 month out
Michelin tables & equals: Venissa (13 Aug — email first, it's their reopening night), Campo del Drago (Sat 15 Aug), La Colombe d'Or lunch (Thu 20 Aug — books like a starred table), La Bastide de Moustiers (21 Aug — children's menu €25–40), Bo.TiC (Sun 23 Aug), SanBrite for the farewell (3 Sep). If you go for Mirazur (20 Aug), book it the moment you commit — free cancellation ends 15 days out, and email them to confirm Aria at dinner.Details and prices in the Dining section.
1 month out
Uffizi timed tickets for Fri 14 Aug afternoon (tickets.uffizi.it, €29 pp advance, Aria free with her own reserved ticket). Mid-August slots go 3–4 weeks out.Closed Mondays — your Friday plan is safe.
3–4 weeks out
Tre Cime toll road reservation for Wed 2 Sep — €40/car and the licence-plate reservation is mandatory (pass.auronzo.info). Also decide Lago di Braies for Thu 3 Sep: arrive before 9:00 (free window) or pre-book parking at pragsparking.com — the access restriction runs to 15 Sep.Rowboats are first-come: shared €15 pp, private ~€50, from 8:00.
1–2 weeks out
The small stuff, all online: Hungary e-vignette (monthly ≈€28 covers both crossings), Slovenia 7-day e-vinjeta €16, Austria 10-day vignette €12.80, Romanian rovinietă; Kayak Vert canoe at Collias for Sun 23 Aug (€27/€14, from age 6); Zambra María la Canastera flamenco for 28 Aug, 20:30 (€26/€20); Dalí Museum timed entry (€22, under-9 free); Oceanogràfic online tickets (€43/€32); Tarot Garden tickets for the 16 Aug afternoon if the mosaic giants beat Siena; Fondation Maeght, Chagall/Matisse and Villa Kérylos tickets online for the 20 Aug art day.One evening with a credit card clears the whole list.
Practical

Small print that saves the day

🪪 Paperwork before you leave

  • Passports/IDs valid well past September; carry them to the Alhambra (checked against tickets) and ferry check-in.
  • Car: green card / insurance confirmation, EU breakdown cover, spare bulbs & vests (mandatory in several countries).
  • Vignettes — buy online the week before: Hungary e-vignette, Slovenia e-vinjeta (outbound), Austria vignette (return). Romania rovinietă as usual.
  • France Crit'Air sticker: Nice's low-emission zone is active in 2026 (weekdays 8:00–20:00, camera-enforced, foreign plates fully in scope). Order only at certificat-air.gouv.fr (~€5 shipped abroad), 4–6 weeks before departure; the email receipt is interim proof.
  • EHIC/CEAM health cards for all three of you.

🚗 Driving quirks by country

  • Italy ZTL: camera-enforced historic-centre zones in Florence, Siena, Pisa, Lucca — always park in a garage/P+R outside the walls. Fines arrive by post a year later.
  • Motorway tolls: Italy ≈ €110–140 across all Italian legs; France ≈ €65–80; Spain's coastal AP-7 is now toll-free. Hungary monthly e-vignette ≈€28 covers both crossings.
  • Spain: most autopistas on your route are now toll-free; Barcelona has a low-emission zone but the port ferry route is on the exempt corridor — still, register the plate online for peace of mind. Ferry boarding day is a Sunday, when the zone isn't enforced — but registration (€7, up to 15 working days) makes any weekday Barcelona driving legal.
  • Fuel up before Alpine passes and before Hungarian borders (cheaper in Slovenia/Hungary than Italy/Austria).

🌡 August realities

  • Andalusia will hit 35 °C+: palaces and museums in the morning, pools and siestas 14:00–18:00, dinners at 21:00 like the locals.
  • 15 Aug is Ferragosto — Italy's biggest holiday. Your itinerary deliberately spends it on farm + villages; book that weekend's tables and rooms first.
  • Water shoes for pebbly Camogli and rocky Costa Brava coves; rash vests save sunscreen wars.
  • Lago di Braies water is ~10 °C even in September. Rowing yes, swimming... heroic.

🎒 The Aria toolkit

  • Museum pacing: 90 minutes max, one "mission" per visit (find Medusa at the Uffizi, count lions at the Alhambra, find the rain-taxi at Dalí's).
  • Audiobook + playlist stack for the two long days; download offline maps for the whole route.
  • Booster seat required everywhere on this route; keep it in the cabin bag rule-of-thumb for the ferry night (cars are inaccessible at sea).
  • A small sketchbook — the trip has a dozen "draw what you see" spots, from Burano to the Cinque Torri trenches.

⏱ Timing traps

  • Nasrid Palaces: your entry window is strict — be inside the Alhambra grounds 30 min early (easy: you're sleeping there).
  • L'Isle-sur-la-Sorgue market is Sunday morning — arrive by 9:30, leave by 11:00.
  • Ferry check-in closes ~1 h before sailing; aim for the port 2½ h ahead.
  • Cortina lifts & the Braies road rules change in early September — the Braies road is restricted 9:00–16:00 through 15 Sep (reserve at pragsparking.com or arrive before 9:00); Faloria and Tofana lifts run to 20/27 Sep, the Cinque Torri chair to 11 Oct.

💶 Money notes

  • Granada's bars still serve a free tapa with each drink — dinner for four can cost the price of four drinks.
  • France: the €25–35 lunchtime menu du jour is how you eat brilliantly on non-event days.
  • Italy: agriturismo dinners (yours does them) are the best value fine food in the country.
  • Hungary/Slovenia fuel is the cheapest of the trip; Monaco parking is not (park at the Oceanographic garage, validate).

The Grand Loop · 12 August – 4 September 2026

Built for M, his wife and Aria — Bucharest → Balaton → Venice lagoon → Val d'Orcia → Liguria → Riviera → Provence → Costa Brava → Valencia → Granada → Altea → Barcelona ⛴ Genoa → San Vito di Cadore → Arad.

Prices, opening hours and schedules were researched in July 2026 and are approximate — always confirm at booking. Drive times are motorway estimates without long stops; August traffic and borders can add 10–20%.
